modules.setup: You're an economic advisor to a state government. GDP has contracted for two straight quarters. The Chief Minister wants your call: are we in a recession?

start.text: The CM wants a yes/no answer right now.

choices.label: Yes — two consecutive quarters of GDP decline is the definition of a recession.
Not necessarily — that's just a common rule of thumb. Check broader activity indicators before declaring it.
Can't say without checking employment data first.

naive.text: You declare a recession. Later, a designated committee reviewing broader indicators disagrees — the two-quarter rule is popular usage, not the official test. Your call looks premature.

nuanced.text: Correct instinct — 'recession' in common usage isn't the same as an official call, which typically weighs multiple indicators, not just two quarters of GDP. Which market do you check first for corroborating signals?

labour.text: Good — the labour market is one of macro's four core markets (goods, bond, money, labour), and unemployment is a direct macro variable. Combined with the output data, you now have enough to advise cautiously rather than declare definitively.

options: The aggregate behavior of the whole economy
